subject.declared_domain: NFRA_GLOBGRPH TO-F2 -- the canonical Kuzu surface guarantee. ensure_fresh() decides whether kuzu_nessie_db is BEHIND Nessie HEAD / stale / unstamped and, if so, rebuilds it BEFORE a caller opens it for query, under a mkdir-mutex with build-to-temp and an atomic swap. Scratch and alternate DBs are explicitly NOT this surface and are never auto-refreshed.

as_of.graph_vintage: Governs the canonical DB rather than holding a vintage of its own. MEASURED live at 03:35:39Z: kuzu_nessie_db built 2026-08-30T01:52:20Z (103.3 min old); its refresh decision keys off _provenance._nessie_head_status against the branch-head marker (measured fresh at 02:11:47Z on card 2), falling through to an age check when the marker is UNKNOWN.

methodology.how: ensure_fresh(db_path, age_warn_hours, rebuild_fn, force) calls needs_refresh() -- which returns True on no manifest ('UNKNOWN VINTAGE'), on _nessie_head_status == 'behind', or on built_at age exceeding age_warn_hours -- then acquires a mutex by os.mkdir (atomic; no flock, per Rule 16 Git Bash). A lock older than ORPHAN_LOCK_S (900 s), or whose heartbeat is staler than HEARTBEAT_STALE_S (90 s) when liveness is on, is STOLEN exactly once; otherwise the loser waits RECHECK_SLEEP_S (2.5 s) and re-checks, reusing a concurrent winner's fresh result, and gives up at MUTEX_WAIT_S (180 s) by writing a refresh-failure and serving the labeled-stale DB. The winner re-checks under the lock (double-checked locking), builds into a temp path, and lands it with an atomic os.replace SWAP guarded by an ownership check so a stolen-from winner never overwrites the stealer's result. Every HANDLED failure (rebuild, mutex-wait, swap) leaves the existing DB in place; a reader never sees a HALF-BUILT NEW DB. The module does not integrity-validate an already-existing DB before serving it stale, and the best-effort sink append is a named exception to the fail-safe guarantee -- see failure_mode.

key.identity_space: FILESYSTEM PATH, reduced to a single basename test. There is exactly one canonical identity and everything else in the same directory is deliberately not it; the sidecars are addressed by suffixing the same db_path, so the whole family shares one root key.
key.key_expression: CANONICAL MEMBERSHIP: is_canonical(db_path) == (os.path.basename(db_path.rstrip('/\\')) == 'kuzu_nessie_db') -- _canonical.py:77-78, verbatim. SIDECAR KEYS are derived from the same root by suffix, each verbatim: lock = db_path.rstrip('/\\') + '.rebuild.lock' (:561); refresh-status = db_path.rstrip('/\\') + _provenance._REFRESH_STATUS_SUFFIX (:108-110); fallback sink = db_path.rstrip('/\\') + _FALLBACK_SINK_SUFFIX (:426-430); TEMP BUILD TARGET is TWO different expressions depending on the liveness flag -- per-unique `f'{base}.rebuild.tmp.{os.getpid()}.{time.monotonic_ns()}.{next(_UNIQ)}'` (:284-288) when live, and the LEGACY shared `db_path.rstrip('/\\') + '.rebuild.tmp'` (:618) when not. A consumer enumerating temp DBs must match BOTH forms or it will miss whichever path the run took.

failure_mode.returns_on_failure: FAIL-SAFE ON ITS HANDLED PATHS, AND UNUSUALLY WELL SIGNALLED -- stated as a BOUNDED claim, not a universal, because this card records its own exception one field below. The HANDLED failures are rebuild, mutex-wait and swap: each leaves the existing, TO-F1-labeled DB in place and returns (False, <reason>). A rebuild exception is caught, the temp DB AND its .wal are removed (so a failed build cannot poison the next rebuild's init), and a refresh-failure marker is written beside the DB. A mutex wait exceeding 180 s writes 'wait-timeout-served-stale' and serves labeled-stale. A swap that cannot land after SWAP_RETRY attempts returns 'swap blocked -- serving existing'. A stolen-from winner's swap ABORTS on the ownership check rather than overwriting the stealer's fresher result, and the finally-release only removes the lock if the caller still owns it. Each labeled-stale path ATTEMPTS a one-line append to .fallback.jsonl so the ambush RATE is observable after the fact -- the append is explicitly best-effort and catches only OSError, so a non-OSError raised while CONSTRUCTING the line is the named exception to the fail-safe guarantee and can propagate into the serve. ⛔ THE INTEGRITY GUARANTEE IS ALSO NARROWER THAN 'never a corrupt DB': what is implemented is that a reader never sees a HALF-BUILT NEW DB (build-to-temp + atomic swap). The module does NOT integrity-validate an ALREADY-EXISTING DB before serving it stale; a DB corrupted by something other than this module's own build path would be served, labeled stale but unvalidated.
silent_degrade_paths: THE #17 LIVENESS INSTRUMENT IS FLAG-GATED OFF BY DEFAULT (:70-74, GLOBGRPH_KUZU_REBUILD_LIVENESS == '1'), and only the comp-kuzu wrappers export it. On any direct-import path the lock carries NO gen token and NO heartbeat, so a slow-live winner and a dead winner are INDISTINGUISHABLE and the only signal left is the 900 s age backstop. MEASURED LIVE at carding: the lock is 25.1 min old, EMPTY, and past that backstop.

verdict.why: This is the most carefully built subject on the face and the card should lead with that. It fails safe on its HANDLED paths -- rebuild, mutex-wait and swap -- rather than warning; it removes a failed build's .wal so the failure cannot poison the next attempt; it checks ownership AT THE SWAP so a stolen-from winner cannot clobber a fresher result, and releases the lock only if it still holds it; it ATTEMPTS a one-line append per labeled-stale serve so the degradation RATE is observable rather than lost to stderr -- best-effort, catching only OSError, so a non-OSError raised while constructing that line is the named exception to the fail-safe guarantee (failure_mode row); and at :112-126 it documents and FIXES exactly the defect class this carding wave exists to find -- a genuine rebuild failure that returned the same value as 'nothing to do', leaving callers unable to distinguish served-stale-because-broken from served-fresh. QUALIFIED rather than SOUND on one coupling, measured live: the #17 rebuild-winner liveness instrument, the per-unique temp path that makes a lock steal harmless, and the reaper for abandoned temps are ALL gated on one environment variable that only the comp-kuzu wrappers export. On any direct-import path the mutex therefore carries no heartbeat, a slow-live winner and a dead one are indistinguishable, and the sole remaining signal is a 900 s age backstop -- which the lock on this box had already exceeded at carding (25.1 min, empty), while 111,874,683 B (106.7 MiB) of temps from 36 h ago sat unreaped because their reaper rides the same flag. Nothing has demonstrably gone wrong; the finding is that the instrument which would tell us is not armed on every path that takes the lock.
